chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Piano lessons in exchange for housework and help from white people
summary: A teacher gave him piano lessons for spring cleaning, and he says he got more help from white than black people; broad exposure shaped his style.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Because I did have some private lessons, in fact there was one time in my life, during that period, that a lady offered to give me piano lessons in exchange to help her do housework in her spring cleaning. She was a teacher. And she had this big house, and I would help her do house cleaning, like you know, ordinary house cleaning.
And I guess she actually would have preferred to have a young boy like me who she wouldn't have to worry about a man molesting her or doing other things, or stealing something.
She figured that I was more in line with someone she could take care of or wouldn't take advantage of her.
And then I did have the talent, and she was interested in me as a musician, and she gave me a few piano lessons in exchange for doing some housework for her.
That was very good, excellent, yes.
So in my life time, as I was speaking of my father, when I first started this conversation, I have been helped by numerous people of the caucasian race.

I would say that it would even balance up to where I've had more help from white people than I've had from black, because I think that unfortunately during my childhood then it was only natural that the caucasian people were in a better position to help because they were more educated, as a whole.
And perhaps had a little more, were in a more fortunate position.

Right. And I think this also has something to do with the style of music that I play. I'm sure it does because like I said, many of the artists who are entertainers, they learn to play from the background of the environment they were raised in, which was limited to an all black community or to circumstances which would not allow them to learn a different type of music. I was exposed to all kinds of music. So it has something to do with the way I play.
